public_rationale: The first part of the claim has support. Utilities were citing data-centre demand to keep fossil plants running before the post; Dominion, for example, dropped its plan to retire a Virginia coal plant in 2023. The IEA later projected natural gas as a lead supplier for AI data centres. But the claim also says this is good for oil-rich countries. I found no evidence measuring any benefit to oil or gas exporters from AI power demand. Oil itself is rarely burned for power. Because one of the two parts is unverified, the claim as a whole is not settled.
limitations: Data-centre demand is not purely generative AI.
Much of the strongest evidence is from 2025, after the post.
The IEA primary report could not be read directly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI uses so much power that it keeps fossil fuels in demand, which benefits oil-rich countries whether or not GenAI ever becomes reliable.
conditions: even if GenAI never becomes reliable

statement.excerpt: (Side bonus: GenAI uses a massive amount of power, to the point of keeping fossil fuels in vogue, and that’s good for oil-rich countries, even if GenAI never becomes reliable.)
statement.document_title: An epidemic of weirdly precise AI butt facts

from_speaker: GenAI uses a massive amount of power
to the point of keeping fossil fuels in vogue
even if GenAI never becomes reliable
our_interpretation: Plain reading has two parts: (1) AI-driven electricity demand is sustaining fossil-fuel power, for example delaying coal or gas plant retirements or driving new gas plants; (2) this benefits oil-rich (fossil-exporting) countries.
The claim describes an ongoing state at the post date. I use the period from 2023 to the post date (2024-10-30), when the AI data-centre boom was visible in utility plans.
'Even if GenAI never becomes reliable' is a hedge, not a condition to test.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that AI data-centre demand was keeping fossil generation in use or expanding it, and that this benefits oil- or gas-exporting countries.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that AI power demand was met without sustaining fossil fuels, or that fossil exporters did not benefit.

evidence.excerpt: It reversed course just three years later. Under its 2023 plan, Dominion projected that its energy demand from data centers would nearly quadruple by 2038.
evidence.locator: section Data Centers Changed Coal's Trajectory, paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Before the post, Dominion reversed its plan to retire the Clover coal plant, citing data-centre demand growth. This supports part (1) of the claim.

evidence.excerpt: renewables and natural gas are set to take the lead due to their cost-competitiveness and availability in key markets.
evidence.explanation: The IEA projects natural gas as a lead supplier for AI data-centre demand, alongside renewables. This is a later projection, so it is context only.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Energy-agency or market analysis that links AI-driven power demand to fossil-fuel export volumes or revenue for oil- and gas-rich countries.
